subject: Harborlane renewal: capacity uplift, price-hold and burst insurance options
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sally Kim <sally.kim@harborlane.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Harborlane renewal: capacity uplift, price-hold and burst insurance options

Hi Sally,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Based on your signal that Harborlane will need a ~25% uplift in monthly embed/generation volume during peak season and you want to keep unit economics predictable, I put together three paths we can take for the renewal:

- 12-month extension (no commit): standard usage rates, short-term price exposure, eligible for burst pool but no price-hold.
- 24-month committed path: 10% volume discount off current list, 6-month price-hold for model family, and a 2% monthly credit bucket applied to overages.
- 24-month committed + burst insurance: 12% volume discount, price-hold for 12 months, and an allocated burst insurance pool (covers up to 40% additional tokens during peak windows).

Attached is a draft termsheet with the above options and a quick example of how pricing changes at different commit levels. Can you confirm which path you want pricing modeled against? If you want, we can also break this into a two-step: sign 24 months at a smaller commit initially and add a planned capacity step-up in month 7.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm preferred path (24-month commit or 24-month + burst).
2) I loop in finance for final pricing and documented credits.
3) We send a termsheet + DocuSign link for electronic signature.

If helpful, I can run a sensitivity with a 30% uplift scenario by EOD Monday.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: Harborlane_Renewal_Termsheet_v2.pdf (PDF, 220 KB)
From: Sally Kim <sally.kim@harborlane.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@harborlane.com
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Harborlane renewal: capacity uplift, price-hold and burst insurance options

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear options. Procurement looped in. A few clarifying Qs before we pick a path:
- Can you give a concrete example of how the 2% monthly credit bucket is applied? Is it refundable or only as account credit?
- For the burst insurance, how fast do we get access to the burst pool and are there any cold-start penalties?

We are leaning toward the committed + burst option but procurement wants the credit mechanics spelled out.

Cc'ing our procurement inbox so they can track the terms.

Thanks,
Sally Kim
Head of Machine Learning Platform, Harborlane Retail
sally.kim@harborlane.com

Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Harborlane renewal: capacity uplift, price-hold and burst insurance options

Hi Sally / Harborlane procurement —

Quick answers and a usage attach to give concrete numbers:

- 2% monthly credit bucket: applied as account credit to invoice line items; non-refundable cashwise but it offsets invoice outstanding balance each billing month. Credits roll forward but expire at contract end. Example: for a $120k invoice, a 2% credit reduces invoice by $2.4k that period.
- Burst insurance mechanics: burst pool is pre-allocated capacity on our Dedicated overlay; when Harborlane signals a burst window (via API flag + Ops page), requests are routed to the burst pool with zero cold-start beyond standard pod spin. There is a per-token surcharge on top of the credit bucket only if usage exceeds burst allocation (we modeled a surcharge in the term sheet — see attachment).

Attached: Usage_Report_Q1_2027.csv — showing baseline month, peak day, and 95th percentile token distribution. Based on that we modeled a 40% burst pool sized to match your historical peaks and show cost delta in the termsheet.

Ben / Lauren — can you confirm: if Harborlane moves to 24-month commit + burst insurance and increases committed volume by 30% vs. current run-rate, we can provide 12% discount plus a one-time 5% onboarding credit (applied to month 1 invoice). Also confirm the credit expiry policy (we propose credits roll forward and expire at contract end).

Sally — if that sounds right I will produce a redline-ready term sheet with DocuSign for procurement.

Thanks,
Jordan

Attachment: Usage_Report_Q1_2027.csv (CSV, 46 KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Harborlane renewal: capacity uplift, price-hold and burst insurance options

Jordan / Lauren —

I reviewed the usage attach and Jordan's ask. Sales is comfortable moving the concession to the 24-month committed + burst insurance path with the following final tweaks:

- Increase discount to 12% (from 10%) conditioned on a 30% committed uplift.
- One-time onboarding credit: 5% applied to first invoice as a bill credit.
- Credit bucket (2% monthly) remains as account credit; credits expire at contract end.
- Add an SLA credit for sustained latency regressions during peak windows (details in the termsheet redline we should circulate).

Lauren — can finance bless the 12% + 5% onboarding credit structure and share any required approval steps for legal to finalize? If finance prefers a step-down discount schedule rather than a flat 12%, say so and we'll model it.

Ben Carter
Senior Director, Sales Operations

Subject: Final: Harborlane 24-month committed + burst insurance — next steps

Hi Sally and Harborlane procurement —

Thanks for the confirmatory signal earlier. Per Ben's note, here are the final commercial bullets we'll put in the redline:

- Term: 24 months
- Commit uplift: 30% above current run-rate (committed vCPU/token volumes captured in SOW)
- Volume discount: 12% off current list when commit met
- Onboarding credit: one-time 5% credit applied to month 1 invoice
- Monthly credit bucket: 2% applied as account credit (rolls forward, expires at contract end)
- Price-hold: 12 months on the specified model family; standard model migration language applies thereafter
- Burst insurance: pre-allocated pool sized to 40% of recent peak; API flag + Ops page for activation; surcharge applies only if burst allocation exceeded
- SLA credit clause: included for sustained latency regressions > 3 standard deviations during peak windows (legal to finalize wording)

Link to redline & DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/harborlane/ds123456789
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890

Procurement — please let me know if this form is acceptable and I will generate the term sheet redline today for signature. If you want a phased commit (start at +15% with a scheduled step-up in month 7 to +30%), we can model that too — it would change discount timing slightly (we can offer a partial pro-rate into the onboarding credit).

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
